subject: Committed wallet: burnlane, escape-hatch and scheduled reconciliation
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@orbitapps.com>, procurement@orbitapps.com
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Committed wallet: burnlane, escape-hatch and scheduled reconciliation

Hi Lena / Orbit procurement team,

Thanks for the time earlier — following up with a compact proposal for the committed wallet structure you asked about. Key design goals we agreed on: predictable unit economics for Q1–Q4 next year, an operational "escape hatch" if usage materially under-indexes the ramp, and a scheduled reconciliation cadence so your finance team can forecast cash flow.

High-level proposal (attached spreadsheet: orbit-proposed-schedule.xlsx):
- 24-month commitment with an annual prepay wallet by year. Year 1: $1.2M prepay (monthly burn target $100k). Year 2: $750k prepay with a step-down discount.
- Burnlane (consumption buckets): monthly buckets with 10% overage buffer. Unused credits expire on annual anniversary unless moved to a grace bucket as described below.
- Escape hatch: a one-time mid-year adjustment window (month 6) allowing a partial refund or credit conversion if trailing 3-month consumption < 60% of committed run-rate. Refund capped at 15% of Year 1 prepay and requires 60 days notice.
- Scheduled reconciliation: monthly usage report + quarterly reconciliation call. Auto-replenishment triggers if remaining wallet < 20% of monthly target; replenishment draws from a reserved buffer at a reduced (rollover) discount level.

Operational items for alignment:
1) Billing cadence (net-30 invoice on prepay drawdown schedule)
2) Audit log access for usage (we can enable token-level exports and a daily CSV)
3) SLAs and fallback model: ability to route to lower-cost model variants during capacity events (discussed separately)

Attachments: orbit-proposed-schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet) — contains monthly run-rate assumptions, amortization table, and two variant scenarios (front-loaded discount vs flat discount).

If that structure looks reasonable I can produce a redline-ready DocuSign package and loop in legal/finance.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

--
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference for teams

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@orbitapps.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: James Hall <james.hall@orbitapps.com>, procurement@orbitapps.com
Date: 2026-12-03T10:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Committed wallet: burnlane, escape-hatch and scheduled reconciliation

Thanks Mateo — reviewed at a high level with procurement and finance. A few clarifying questions before we escalate to legal:

1) Escape hatch mechanics: how is the 60% threshold calculated (rolling 3 months vs trailing 6 months)? We prefer trailing 6 months to avoid transient dips triggering refunds.
2) Refund mechanics: does the refund include fees or is it gross prepay pro rata? Is the 15% cap negotiable if we commit a larger Year 2 top-up?
3) Rollover buffer: can unused credits be reallocated to other internal orgs under the same account instead of expiring? We have two business units that might share the wallet.
4) Audit evidence: procurement requires a compact procurement questionnaire and SOC2 evidence pointer for the data-retention policy — attached (orbit-procurement-questions.pdf).

Also please provide an amortization example showing how refunds and reallocation would appear on our ledger (we want month-by-month journal entries).

Appreciate the clear bullets — copying Legal (James) and Finance (procurement@orbitapps.com).

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Procurement, Orbit Apps
lena.ortiz@orbitapps.com

Attachments: orbit-procurement-questions.pdf (procurement questionnaire)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@orbitapps.com>, procurement@orbitapps.com
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Committed wallet: burnlane, escape-hatch and scheduled reconciliation

Hi Lena — thanks, good questions. Quick answers and next steps below; attached is a short amortization extract in the spreadsheet (see sheet: "Amortization + Refund Examples").

Responses:
- Threshold window: we can switch to a trailing 6-month lookback for the escape-hatch calculation. Operationally we'll compute average monthly consumption over the trailing 6 months and compare to the committed monthly target.
- Refund mechanics: refunds are gross prepay pro rata less any consumed token charges. The 15% cap is a starting point; if you front-load Year 2 (>= $1M) we can increase cap to 25% and soften the rollback fee.
- Reallocation: yes — credits can be scoped at account or sub-account level. We support intra-account reallocation with an admin approve flow (we'll add that to the SOW).
- Audit evidence: pointer to SOC2 report and token-level export options included in the related links — we can provide a signed SOC2 AOC under NDA.

Amortization example (excerpt):
- Month 1: Prepay $1,200,000 booked to deferred revenue; monthly recognized usage entry for $100,000 at point of consumption.
- Month 6 low-usage case: trailing 6-month average = $55,000 (55% of target) -> eligible escape-hatch. Refund calculation: (Committed remaining balance * pro rata %) capped at agreed percent. Example line: eligible refund = min(remaining_balance * pro-rata, 15% * Year1_prepay).

Operational checklist for final SOW:
1) Confirm trailing window (6 months) — orbit approves
2) Confirm refundable cap (15% or 25% if Year 2 front-loaded)
3) Select account scope for reallocation (account-level vs BU-level)
4) Sign SOW + attach procurement questionnaire answers + SOC2 AOC under NDA

I'll attach a redline-ready agreement and a DocuSign link once you confirm points 1–3. Also linking the HubSpot deal for internal tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/6789012/ORBIT-2026-11-20.

Thanks,
Mateo

Attachments: orbit-proposed-schedule.xlsx (see "Amortization + Refund Examples" sheet)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@orbitapps.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Committed wallet: burnlane, escape-hatch and scheduled reconciliation

Lena — quick note from Redwood finance/sales ops.

We can confirm the trailing 6-month escape-hatch window and the intra-account reallocation option. Regarding the refundable cap: if Orbit agrees to a Year 2 front-load of >= $1M, Redwood will move to a 25% refund-cap and reduce the rollback fee to 2.5% of refunded amount.

Next steps we propose (simple checklist):
- Orbit: confirm window (6 months), scope (account-level reallocation OK), and Year 2 intent (front-load amount or not).
- Redwood: produce redline + DocuSign package and provide SOC2 AOC under NDA.
- Target: sign SOW by 2027-01-10 to lock preferred pricing.

I've attached the DocuSign draft for signatures: redwood-docusign-agreement.docx (will be pushed to the DocuSign link upon acceptance).

If those points are acceptable, we can have legal exchange redlines next week.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
